# Learning

I am happiest in my work when I am learning new things. My core desire in terms of my career is to know that I have continued to learn throughout. Having an inquisitive mind for topics that interest me makes me a strong researcher. I also understand that whilst needing to work within the parameters of a client's business it is often beneficial to question the _status quo_ and suggest new ways of looking for solutions.   

# Being open

I use open source software almost exclusively on my computers. I preferentially use open data for the majority of my work. If possible, I push for data I generate, or code I write, to be made available under a permissive or copy-left licence. I also prefer to approach project delivery using open and collaborative methods.

# Ethics

I don't work for organisations or projects that are directly linked to the oil & gas or defence sectors. I don't fly on environmental grounds. I try to work with teams and on projects that align with my environmental principles and views around a fair society. This does not limit my ability to work, and directs me towards work designed to make a positive difference.

## AI

AI as a term is being used as a catch all. Domain specific models such as those used for assessing ecology or remotely sensed data have a huge amount of utility in improving the speed and robustness of analysis. I am happy to work with these models and to use them in my work. However, I recognise the huge potential risks associated with big-tech's large language models (LLMs). I would be happy to have a conversation about the use of LLMs to discuss the risks and benefits of their use. Working with specific, smaller, greener LLMs where appropriate is something I am interested in exploring.
